To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified the type 2 diabetes susceptibility gene TCF7l2 as a major determinant of normal variation in birth weight and that this association is driven by the effect of the maternal genotype.

1) the TCF7L1/2 gene is associated with birth weight, 2) this is driven by the maternal genotype, 3) this is likely due to the maternal genotype reducing insulin secretion in pregnancy, and 4) the maternal genotype is likely the cause of the association, not the fetal genotype.
the TCF7L.2 gene, which predisposes to type 2 diabetes, increases offspring birth weight by increasing maternal blood glucose concentrations during pregnancy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying genes that influence birth weight and the mechanisms by which they do so.
the role of the TCF7L1 gene, a recently discovered gene that is associated with the common form of diabetes, in the regulation of birth weight.
understanding the genetic and environmental causes of birth-weight variation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TCF7L.2 gene is associated with type 2 diabetes and that this association has been shown to have an effect on the birth weight of the offspring.
a common variant in TCF7L1, rs7903146, has been identified that influences birth weight by altering maternal glucose metabolism in pregnancy.
the TCF7L1L2 gene has been found to be associated with birth weight, and this association may have an impact in the development of diabetes later in life.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fetal TCF7LL2 genotype is not associated with birth weight, but the maternal TCF7Ll2 genotype is.
TCF7L.2 is the first diabetes gene to be associated with birth weight, and the association is mediated through maternal genotype.

TCF7L.2 genotype in the fetus is not associated with birth weight, but maternal genotype is, and this is due to reduced maternal insulin secretion and hence increased maternal glycemia during pregnancy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetic component to normal birth-weight variation can be substantial.
common gene variants can substantially alter normal birth-weight variation and that these variants may be useful in understanding the biology of fetal growth.
the risk of diabetes is not only determined by the genetic risk of the offspring.
